deploy-bot: Deploy check FAILED for release r2026.3 — blocking promotion :warning:
deploy-bot: Problem summary: environment layer mismatch between staging and prod for service `inference-cache`.
deploy-bot: Diff (extracted from preflight):
```
staging: S3_CACHE_PREFIX=s3://ri-staging-inference/cache/v2/
prod:    S3_CACHE_PREFIX=s3://ri-prod-inference/cache/v1/
staging: KEYSTORE_PATH=/keystore/inference/staging/
prod:    KEYSTORE_PATH=/keystore/inference/
secret schema: staging has JSON object for `cache/credentials`, prod has base64 string
kms_alias: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/ri-staging != arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/ri-prod
```
deploy-bot: Impact flagged: model cache misses and cache lookup errors -> potential 5xx spike. Release PAUSED, rerun after manual resolution.

maria: Ack. How likely is this to cause a rollout-wide outage vs just degraded cache hit rate?

josh: If prod keeps v1 prefix, newly warmed entries from this deploy will write to v2 and prod will read v1 -> cold lookups + higher downstream latency. Not immediate 5xx but sustained latency and higher cost.

anna: We can either normalize prefixes (backfill/alias) or change config on the new deployment to point at v1. Quickest is patching the deployment env var for the canary.

kevin: Patch sounds safer than rollback. But if we point new pods at v1, we need to confirm key path access (keystore + kms). The keystore path difference worries me. Is it just a trailing segment?

josh: Keystore path mismatch is semantic — code resolves absolute path concatenation. If we change prefix without migrating keys you'll get 403 from KMS in some calls. Need key mapping/alias.

maria: Decision call: hold full rollout. Immediate actions: 1) anna to open a small canary config PR to point canary at prod prefixes; 2) josh to run a targeted canary after PR; 3) kevin to validate KMS/keystore permissions; 4) create ticket for prefix normalization/migration. Change window ends in 45m.

anna: On it — will open PR now for deployment/inference CANARY env override. Patch snippet:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/inference-canary S3_CACHE_PREFIX=s3://ri-prod-inference/cache/v1/ KEYSTORE_PATH=/keystore/inference/
```
I will include a migration job (one-shot) to map v2 -> v1 keys if we go that route.

kevin: I'll run a quick dry auth check against the keystore path and kms alias (takes ~10m). If auth ok, canary with prod prefix is acceptable. If not, rollback to previous image is preferred.

sre-oncall: Adding monitoring steps: watch `cache.read.misses`, `inference.latency.p50`, `5xx.rate`. I'll pin a short-term alert threshold and page if 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 3m.

josh: After PR merges, I'll kick off the canary run and share logs here. If canary passes for 10m with healthy cache metrics, we can either proceed or run the migration job during the next maintenance window.

maria: Thanks. I'll update the release notes and notify PM/ops about the hold and the migration ticket. No rollback for now unless canary fails. :eyes:

anna: PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/PR/4123 — includes env override + migration job stub + docs.

deploy-bot: Noted — will re-run preflight on PR merge and unblock automatically if checks pass.

maria: Closing loop: hold release, canary-only change, validate keys, then decide migration vs gradual switchover. Assigning owners in ticket.

kevin: I'll post results of the kms auth check in ~8m.

josh: will start canary once anna's PR is merged.

sre-oncall: Monitoring configured. Standing by. :mag:
